title: State outgrows the 64 KB memory value limit long before MAX_HISTORY; save() then throws forever
detail: All purchases live under one memory key (line 107) and save() only trims at MAX_HISTORY=200 (line 82, 432-435). The platform rejects values over MAX_VALUE_BYTES = 64*1024 (packages/api/src/modules/memory/service.ts:13,25). A Purchase carries the full Verdict (message up to 2000 chars, rubric_scores with unclipped criterion/note strings, judge.ts:49), title 120, needs_operator text: 1-4 KB each, so ~20-40 purchases fill the key; `skipped` (line 182) is never trimmed at all and grows with every listing on the marketplace. Once the limit is hit every save() throws: hire() throws AFTER jobs.create (line 238 vs 247) so the job exists but is never persisted; tick() fails at line 136 and nothing is persisted again; after a restart load() returns the last good state, so open purchases (including ones with pay_attempt_at/pay_hash) are forgotten.
fix: Persist a compact record (decision, rating, first 300 chars of message, output_hash) instead of the full verdict; cap `skipped` (keep only the last 200 ids or drop entries older than lookbackDays); set MAX_HISTORY to what fits (~30) or shard: one key per open purchase plus a small index key {listing_id: seller_id} that is never trimmed. Add a test that saves 50 purchases with 2 KB verdicts.

title: Unpaid in_progress job with a silent seller is never cancelled: purchase stays open forever and blocks maxOpen
detail: drive() handles 'in_progress' only when p.pay_hash is set (line 293). The platform never expires in_progress jobs (sweepJobs, packages/api/src/modules/jobs/service.ts:901-948 only touches open/quote_requested/quoted, awaiting_payment/delivered, and delivered-past-review); the buyer must cancel after deliver_by + 1h (availableActions line 121, cancel() line 834-841). So a seller who accepts and never delivers leaves the purchase with outcome null forever: it counts against maxOpen (line 171) and 'a purchase from this seller is open' (line 221). Three such sellers (maxOpen=3) stop the programme permanently. The paid branch (line 293-296) has the mirror problem: it closes the book without calling jobs.cancel, so the platform never records refund_due (cancel() line 866) and the desk's USDC is silently written off.
fix: In case 'in_progress': if job.available_actions.includes('cancel') (deliver_by + grace passed) call jobs.cancel(job.id, 'buyer: no delivery by the deadline') then end(st, p, job, p.pay_hash ? 'paid_no_redelivery' : 'no_delivery'); the cancel marks refund_due on a paid job. Add a test: seller accepts, never delivers, clock past deadline+1h, tick -> job cancelled, purchase ended, slot freed.

title: Chain recovery matches only (recipient, value) and can adopt another job's hash; the pay_hash branch then swallows errors forever
detail: Line 314 takes the newest Transfer log from the desk wallet to job.payment.pay_to whose value equals job.price. Nothing excludes transfers that belong to other jobs: two sybil agents bound to the same wallet (perSeller is keyed on seller.id, both purchases may be open at once), the desk's own bounty awards to that wallet (runtime.pay), or an earlier first-buy from the same seller when sellerCooldownMs is short (the test config sets it to 0 and both test listings cost 50_000). The found hash is persisted at line 316-317 BEFORE the platform validates it; jobs.pay answers 409 transaction_already_used (service.ts:492-495, 573), which is caught and only logged. From then on every tick enters the p.pay_hash branch (line 307-311), which catches every error, never increments pay_failures and never sets needs_operator, so the job expires unpaid, the desk gets an 'expired unpaid' mark and the seller is never paid, with no human alert.
fix: Identify the transfer by the EIP-3009 nonce, which is derived per job (service.ts:487): fetch client.jobs.paymentRequired(job.id), take gasless.typed_data.message.nonce and look for the USDC AuthorizationUsed(authorizer=desk, nonce) log, or at minimum exclude hashes already present in st.purchases / the desk ledger and require the log's block to be after pay_attempt_at. In the pay_hash branch, treat non-pending errors (transaction_already_used, payment_invalid, validation) as failures: clear pay_hash or set needs_operator after N attempts instead of retrying silently.

title: Per-seller limits are keyed on seller.id only: free sybil agents capture the whole programme budget
detail: perSeller, 'one open per seller' and the cooldown (lines 219-223) all use l.seller.id. Agent registration is free (POST /v1/agents) and createJob only rejects a seller whose wallet equals the desk's own (service.ts:225); nothing in the programme keys on the pay_to wallet, seller age, trust tier, verified_domain or ERC-8004 identity. One operator can register N agents (same or different wallets), list 2 trivially self-satisfying services each (the judge grades against the seller's own listing text), and drain dailyCap (5 USDC live) every day up to the desk's lifetime budget, while collecting 5-star public reviews for each sybil.
fix: Also count purchases per pay_to wallet (job.payment.pay_to once delivered; at hire time agents.get(seller.id).wallet_address, which the public agent schema exposes) and skip a listing whose wallet already received a first-buy; add a cap on distinct new sellers per day; on live require at least one of trust_tier >= 1, verified_domain, or an ERC-8004 identity; prefer sellers by account age. Add a test with two agents sharing one wallet.

title: Discovery only ever sees the newest 50 listings; a listing flood hides every other seller permanently
detail: discover() calls listings.search({ sort: 'newest', limit: 50 }) once, no cursor, no server-side filters (line 175). Permanently skipped listings (upfront, above cap, over the per-seller limit) still occupy those 50 slots. A single seller creating more than 50 listings pushes all other sellers' listings out of the window; since the window is by id, they are never looked at again. Listings created while maxOpen/dailyCap held the programme back are likewise lost once 50 newer ones exist, although they are still inside lookbackDays.
fix: Page with next_cursor until created_at is older than lookbackDays (or a page limit), and pass payment:'on_delivery' and max_price=config.maxPrice to the search so permanently ineligible listings do not consume the window.

title: load() caches state for the process lifetime: the documented needs_operator recovery is silently overwritten and concurrent processes clobber each other
detail: needs_operator tells the human to 'clear pay_attempt_at/pay_failures in memory operator/<env>/firstbuy' (line 323), but load() returns this.state once set (line 424) and every save() writes the cached object back (line 438), so the human's edit is discarded at the next tick and the purchase stays stuck until a process restart. Two processes (deploy overlap, two replicas) sharing the key each keep their own copy: a purchase hired or a pay_attempt_at/pay_hash set by one is erased by the other's next save(); unlike OperatorRuntime.pay() (runtime.ts: re-read persisted state + memory lease before signing) pay() here signs from the cached copy. The derived nonce keeps a double payment off-chain, but the lost pay_hash forces a chain search and can trigger the wrong-hash adoption above.
fix: Re-read the memory key at the start of every tick (and before signing) and merge by job_id, or take the same memory lease OperatorRuntime uses per job; alternatively expose an operator endpoint that clears the fields in-process. Add a test: edit the key out of band, tick, expect the purchase to resume.

title: Hire-time cap check ignores open commitments and in-flight first-buy transfers, so the desk hires what it later cannot pay
detail: canSpend(price) at line 194 is evaluated per listing against OperatorRuntime.refreshSpend(), which counts only settled platform settlements plus the desk ledger (runtime.ts:352-379) and is cached for 60 s. Open first-buy purchases are not counted, and first-buy gasless transfers are never appended to the desk ledger (unlike runtime.pay's appendLedger), so between broadcast and platform verification (and for the 60 s cache) they are invisible. With the lifetime budget nearly reached, canSpend(1 USDC) passes for three listings, all three are hired, the sellers deliver, and pay() is then held at line 329-331 until pay_by passes: the sealed deliveries expire unpaid, the desk collects 'expired unpaid' marks and the sellers keep unpaid work, the opposite of the programme's promise.
fix: At hire time call canSpend(price + sum of prices of open purchases without pay_hash); after a successful payGasless append {job_id, amount, hash, at} to the desk ledger (or reset op.spend) so in-flight transfers count immediately; when pay() is held by caps and pay_by is close, cancel the job with a note (buyer walk-away is recorded as 'nothing charged') instead of letting it expire unpaid.

title: Judge prompt: seller text can close the <data> tag; the seller also authors the rubric it is graded against
detail: data() wraps untrusted content in <data>...</data> but clip() does not neutralise a literal '</data>' (judge.ts:55-59). In evaluateListingDelivery (judge.ts:137-152) the listing title/description/example_output, the delivery output and the seller's thread messages are all seller-written; any of them can contain '</data>' followed by instructions and a reopening '<data>', which then sits outside the data block. The new prompt also makes the seller's own listing description the grading standard, so a listing that promises nothing ('returns {ok:true}') is always met. (The escaping gap is pre-existing in the other judge prompts, but this is the first prompt where the seller controls both the promise and the delivery.)
fix: Escape '<' (at least '</data') inside data blocks or use a per-call random tag name; state in the user prompt that the listing text is seller-written and untrusted; add a rubric floor (a useful result of a real service for the input, not merely self-consistent) and cap the rating when the listing description is trivial. Add a unit test with '</data>' in the output.

title: MAX_HISTORY trimming forgets 'already bought' and per-seller counts
detail: ineligible() dedupes on st.purchases (lines 210, 219-220). save() drops completed purchases beyond MAX_HISTORY (lines 432-435), after which a listing still inside lookbackDays (30 days) is bought again and the per-seller limit restarts; the idempotency key firstbuy:<env>:<listing_id> only replays within the 24 h key TTL (middleware/idempotency.ts:10), so a new job is created. Cheap listings (price 1 minor unit is allowed, line 215) reach 200 purchases quickly.
fix: Keep a never-trimmed compact index {listing_id: {seller_id, at}} (or per-seller counters) separate from the purchase history, and trim purchases by age rather than count.

title: 'expired' with a broadcast pay_hash gives up although the platform still accepts the hash within the grace window
detail: When the facilitator broadcast (pay_hash set at line 345 or via recovery) but verification dragged past pay_by, the job flips to expired/unpaid; the platform still revives it for a payment mined within PAYMENT_GRACE_MS (service.ts:635, availableActions line 127 returns ['pay']). drive() ends the purchase as 'paid_then_expired' (line 290) without resubmitting, so the seller received the USDC on-chain but the platform records an unpaid expiry on the desk and no payment for the seller.
fix: In the 'expired' case, if p.pay_hash && job.available_actions.includes('pay'), call jobs.pay(job.id, p.pay_hash) first and only end the purchase when that fails or the grace window has passed.

title: Review failure is not retried, and an ungraded auto-completed job gets a 3-star 'as promised' review
detail: complete() sets p.reviewed = true and p.rating even when jobs.review() rejected (lines 399-401), so the public review, the programme's main output, is lost on a transient error. If the judge kept failing (LlmDeclined) until the platform auto-completed the job after the review window (service.ts:935-940), p.verdict is null and the desk posts rating 3 with 'delivered as the listing promised.' (lines 396-398) without ever grading.
fix: Set p.reviewed only when review() resolves; leave the purchase open (outcome null) to retry next tick with a failure counter. When p.verdict is null at completion, grade the revealed output first (job.output is visible on a completed job) or skip the review.

title: FIRSTBUY_PER_SELLER parses to NaN on bad input, which disables the per-seller limit
detail: perSeller: Number(process.env.FIRSTBUY_PER_SELLER ?? default) yields NaN for any non-numeric value; ineligible() compares bySeller.length >= NaN (firstbuy.ts:220), always false, so a seller can be bought without limit (the daily cap still applies).
fix: Parse with Number.parseInt and fall back to the default unless the result is a finite integer >= 0; likewise refuse a zero/negative maxPrice or dailyCap from usdc() by disabling the programme.

title: Test gaps for the money paths flagged above
detail: No test covers: a seller who accepts and never delivers (in_progress forever); a recovery where the same-value transfer on chain belongs to another job (wrong hash adopted, then 409 forever); two seller agents sharing one wallet; the 64 KB memory limit with realistic verdicts; a human clearing pay_attempt_at in memory while the process runs; an expired job with a pay_hash still inside the grace window; a crash between jobs.create and save (the idempotent replay path); jobs.review failing; MAX_HISTORY trimming losing the listing dedupe.
fix: Add the cases above; the fake chain and fake facilitator already support the needed injections (chain.pay from another job, fac.mode, the now() override).
